name: Austronesian expansion out of Taiwan
short_desc: Seafaring Austronesian-speaking communities spread from Taiwan into island Southeast Asia and, over later centuries, across the Pacific and to Madagascar.
date_note: Circa 2000 BCE marks the approximate outward expansion from Taiwan. Pacific islands and Madagascar were reached in later, different regional phases.
notes: Added after a catalog gap review on 24 October 2026. Connects otherwise isolated Madagascar and New Zealand settlement entries to a major maritime dispersal across the Indian and Pacific oceans. Evidence and date rationale: Circa 2000 BCE is a rounded marker for departure from Taiwan, corresponding to the cited 2014 study’s estimate of roughly 4,000 years ago. It is not the date when all later destinations were reached. Later Pacific and Madagascar settlements follow different regional chronologies; migrations involved interaction with existing populations. Primary evidence: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3951936/. Cached Wikipedia introduction and lead image provide separately attributed background. Remains review, not comprehensive factual approval.
